bottom_line.headline: Three contested ADVANCE names, CAKE, DRI and DIS, all fresh breakouts to new highs, into a RISK OFF downtrend tape with dealers short gamma; three more were dropped and the book is flat.
bottom_line.paragraph: This is the fourth Committee Standard Scan: the analysts picked from all 1,617 universe names with no AQE gate, and every name that reached the slate is on AQE's Longlist and Elder list anyway. The market kill line, the index logging 4 to 5 distribution days inside 4 to 5 weeks, already reads as crossed on the stage layer's count of 8 in 25 sessions, so rule on it before any trigger. Nothing is held: SPCX closed on 18 Nov and RBRK was stopped on 17 Nov.

RISK OFF for five days, trend regime DOWNTREND; the handbook's doctrine is that breadth is against the tape, so build the watchlist and do not push new entries. A reading, not an Aegis rule.

weather.stance: Read: Valen's stance is RISK OFF now and five days ago, against NEUTRAL a month ago, and the trend regime has been DOWNTREND at all three points. SPY and QQQ have neither a daily nor a weekly buy signal and neither sits above a rising 5-day line; SPY is 2.86 daily ranges under its 50-day and QQQ 3.41, and VIX/VIX3M is 1.05, above the 1.00 stress line. Handbook doctrine, not an Aegis rule: breadth is against the tape, build the watchlist, do not push new entries.
weather.gex: Read: the light is RED. SPY at 730.20 sits 3.11% under the 752.91 flip, with the put wall at 725 (0.71% below) and the call wall at 775 (6.14% above), so dealers amplify moves both ways; reclaiming the flip calms the tape and losing 725 removes the cushion. QQQ at 659.51 is 2.72% under its 677.48 flip and already under its 680 put wall, call wall 700. Dealer side is the standard assumption, not observed data.
weather.heartbeat: Read: the average stock has kept up with the index for 23 days (broadening): +5.28% over 20 days, +1.89% over 60 and +0.68% over the last 5, confidence 0.75, at the top of its 12-month range, so the phase is late rather than early. The ratio sits 1.55% above its 20-day average (0.2904) and 1.28% under its 12-month high (0.2988); a cross under that average would turn it before the label changes.
weather.positioning: Read: trend funds are neutral across 18 markets with none at an extreme (dial 1.00), leaning long currencies (+0.59) and short metals (-0.49) and rates (-0.38), slightly short stocks (-0.10). Nearest lines: they turn buyers of the Dow above 50,468.14 (0.42% above), of the 2-year note above 102.87 (0.96% above) and of the Russell 2000 above 2,772.24 (1.82% above); they turn sellers of Brent below 88.92 (2.75% below).
weather.volatility: Read: VIX at 24.56 is higher than 91% of days in two years and 0.44 points under the 25 line where protection is already expensive; VIX/VIX3M is 1.05, up from 1.01 five days ago and 0.97 a month ago, and the curve is in backwardation. Single stocks imply 48.56, a gap of 23.10 that is wider than 74% of the past two years but narrowing (-0.84 points in 20 days), 2.87% under its elevated band at 23.76; these readings are as of 17 Nov, and implied correlation is 23.24.
weather.divergence: Read: Valen counts 0 of 8 market-level warning types fired, and Crown's summary says no warning signs are lit while its count shows 3 with none named. No single one is a reason to sell; they matter when several agree with breadth, and breadth is still labelled broadening.
weather.call: Read: Crown's family is broadening carry, a partial fit at a 1.00x multiplier on the PM's own risk (a reading, not a size): breadth broadening, the stock-level gap normal and trend funds near a low flip are met, while breadth not at an extreme and dealers long gamma both fail. The leading macro story is a dollar squeeze with 93.14% of its conditions met at full coverage, not contested, runner-up a growth scare. Next tests: jobless claims 19 Nov 08:30 ET, ISM manufacturing and services 23 Nov, core PCE, claims and durable goods 25 Nov.
weather.cot: Read: big speculators are crowded long small caps (Russell 2000), the 30-year bond and the 5-year note, and crowded short natural gas and silver. The small-cap crowding is the one that matters for a stock book, as context and not timing, with small caps 1.82% under the level where trend funds turn buyers; the report covers 10 Nov and the next is due 20 Nov.
weather.checklist: Read: nothing on the checklist passes: today's count is not green, the 5-day up/down 4% count is 0.44 against the 1.00 pass, net new highs trail (8-day average 2.88 against 22.0 over 20 days) and monthly big risers are 53. Above their 20-day line 20.2%, 50-day 33.7%, 200-day 36.8% and 40-day 34.8%: about a third of stocks hold the medium lines, counts the file labels as US-listed stocks over $2B, not AQE's own list.
weather.turning: Read: stance RISK OFF now and five days ago against NEUTRAL a month ago; stocks above their 40-day line 34.8% against 47.6% and 51.5%; SPY -2.86 daily ranges from its 50-day against -0.47 and +0.11; VIX/VIX3M 1.05 against 1.01 and 0.97, so the weather has worsened on every gauge. Stocks above their 40-day line clearing 50 or the 5-day count clearing 1.00 (now 0.44, already under the 0.70 warning line) would turn it, and the 350 monthly-risers line is a whole-market count (now 53), not a target on AQE's list.
weather.themes: Read: on Valen's 96 baskets the true leaders on both horizons and near their highs are Restaurants (+0.69% on the week, +9.51% on the month, 4.86% under its high), Advertising Technology (3.98% under), Specialty Retail (2.02% under), Cruise and Pharmaceuticals; Car Dealers, Airlines and Homebuilding are bounces off the floor 17.6% to 19.1% under their highs. The biggest weekly turns, Brazil, Argentina and Oil and Gas Downstream, are falling less this week than this month in groups 28% to 40% under their highs, broken groups and not leaders.
weather.groups: Read: the turning sectors are Technology (APP, BILL, VIA) and Communication Services (LFTO, LBTYK, CHTR, home of DIS), and the turning themes with two or more strong names are Social Media (APP, TTD) and AI Software (APP, SAIL). Further along and already leading: Consumer Discretionary (36 strong names, including WWW, VIK and the restaurant pair), Consumer Staples and Utilities, with Travel Leisure and Transport Logistics among the themes; a place to look, not a list to buy.
